summary.headline: Sudeep Pharma Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to INR196.7 crore with EBITDA margin of 37.2%, a record quarter despite Fortified Rice pause.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA, with revenue up 21% YoY and 24% QoQ, and EBITDA margin up about 310 bps YoY to 37.2%. Pharma Food Nutrition (PFN) drove growth, rising 57% YoY, while Specialty Ingredients fell 25% YoY after the Government's Fortified Rice programme paused. PAT grew only 11% YoY to INR51.8 crore because of lower other income, a higher effective tax rate of 27%, and new greenfield depreciation. Management guided to positive YoY growth in Specialty Ingredients in Q3 and Q4 and kept the Dahej battery-materials start date of April 2027.

segments.name: Pharma Food Nutrition (PFN)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR142 crore, +57% YoY, about 72% of consolidated revenue; segment EBITDA margin about 41% vs 33% a year ago, and segment EBITDA nearly doubled. Growth came from phosphates and magnesium bisglycinate, with volume up about 30-35% in the quarter per management.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients
segments.commentary: Revenue INR54 crore, +9% QoQ but -25% YoY; segment margin about 28%, down YoY. Fortified Rice programme pause removed a contribution that was about 20-25% of segment revenue (about INR40-50 crore in FY26), and NSS was softer.

segments.name: Sudeep Advanced Materials (battery materials, Dahej)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 capacity of 25,000 tpa battery-grade iron phosphate; commercial operations targeted April 2027, with binding offtake update expected in Q4 FY27. Phase 2 targets 100,000 tpa and expansion to 200,000 tpa is being discussed. Capex for the Dahej project was part of FY27 capex of about INR77 crore.

segments.name: NSS (within Specialty)
segments.commentary: Management expects a flat FY27; five customer approvals and about 12 projects at evaluation stages. Target is growth in line with the core business in FY28 and an EBITDA margin near 30%.

guidance_outlook: Specialty Ingredients expected to return to positive YoY growth in Q3 and Q4 FY27, based on new customer contracts and excluding any Fortified Rice restart.
Specialty margin expected to recover toward pre-Q2 levels in Q3 and Q4, per management.
Working capital target of about 170-180 days excluding battery inventory in FY27, and about 150 days over the longer term.

Greenfield Nandesari plant (51,000 tpa, FDA approved last week) expected to contribute revenue mainly from Q4 FY27; utilisation of about 10-15% in FY28, and about 75% at maturity in 3-4 years with about 3x asset turnover.
Magnesium bisglycinate targeted to become a top-3 PFN revenue contributor within 2-3 years, with potential of at least INR100 crore.
Margins expected to be sustained at current levels, but greenfield operating costs and battery costs will start hitting the P&L as commissioning nears.
Binding offtake details for the battery business expected in the next call or within two months.
capex_capacity: Greenfield Nandesari facility capitalised in Q2 FY27 and received US FDA approval; 51,000 tpa annual capacity covering phosphates, glycinates, gluconates and citrates. Commercial supply expected in H2 FY27 with revenue mainly from Q4.

Existing Nandesari PFN site operating at close to optimum utilisation, about 80%. About 40% of Nandesari capacity is allocated to other products, and management expects 70-80% of that to go to magnesium bisglycinate.
Specialty Ingredients utilisation around 40-45% in FY26, expected to recover to about 40-45% by Q4 FY27.

Dahej battery plant: Phase 1 of 25,000 tpa commercial operations from April 2027; scale-up to 100,000 tpa and then 200,000 tpa. Management referred to about INR600 crore capex for the first 100,000 tpa.
FY27 capex about INR77 crore, mainly battery project at Dahej and greenfield completion. Battery inventory is being built up ahead of commissioning.
demand_pricing: Phosphoric acid prices rose about 40% vs Q4 FY26 by Q1 FY27 and strengthened further; pass-through was executed and Q1 inventory built ahead of price increases supported Q2 and October-November.
Management does not expect margins to strengthen further at current levels until the next contracting cycle.
Freight costs were elevated; selling and distribution costs were about INR8 crore above the normal quarterly average, absorbed without passing on to customers.
Magnesium bisglycinate realisation is about 2-3x the PFN average; the company has about 8-9 US approvals and about 30-35 approvals globally. Commercial supply is limited to select customers until Q4.

Battery-grade iron phosphate: China produces nearly 100% of global supply (about 5 million tons). Sudeep positions itself as an ex-China supplier at a slight premium, linked to US 45X PFE-compliant supply requirements.
Export share about 65% of revenue (exports up 24% YoY), domestic about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is Specialty Ingredients underlying growth excluding Fortified Rice, and what growth is expected in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fortified Rice was about 20-25% of segment revenue (INR40-50 crore in FY26). Premix was hit by product mix change even though volumes grew. Non-Fortified Rice premix contracts for Q3 and Q4 are expected to largely offset the loss.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Specialty margin fall while PFN margins rose sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to operating leverage: premix, a large contributor, had limited revenue, and NSS was a drag. Q3 and Q4 contracts are expected to carry better margins than the Fortified Rice business they replace.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PFN growth from volume or pricing, and what is the PFN volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came mainly from phosphates (up about 70-80%) and magnesium bisglycinate, which received the maximum capacity allocation in the existing setup. PFN volume grew about 30-35% in Q2 and about 19% in H1.

qa_highlights.question: How will bisglycinate be distributed across customers, and how much of Nandesari capacity can go to it?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of bisglycinate volume will go to larger customers, including two of the largest US tolling manufacturers, and 50% to mid/small customers, to avoid concentration. About 70-80% of the 40% of capacity allocated to other products would go to bisglycinate; the remaining 60% of the greenfield is mainly phosphates and is not easily fungible.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Phase 1 battery capacity is covered by binding offtake agreements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give volume detail today, saying the company would break it out by customer and volume at the next call or within two months. Binding commitments are targeted for Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the battery pricing premium and return profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is set at a slight premium to China, driven by US 45X PFE-compliant supply rules, and capped by competitiveness. Management targets asset turns of about 3x and ROCE similar to the core business, and will not guide EBITDA margin for the battery business.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Phase 1 plant approval needed for Korean customers, and how long does validation take?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant approval for the Dahej site is expected to take 3-6 months because product and process approval is already in place. Management assumes about half a year of FY28 for commercial supply and revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NSS revenue and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is expected to be flat. FY28 growth should be similar to the core business, and the NSS target EBITDA margin is close to 30% after supply chain changes.

risks_watch: Fortified Rice programme restart is uncertain; management has no visibility on whether it resumes in FY27.
Specialty Ingredients must return to positive YoY growth in Q3 and Q4 FY27 on new contracts. Watch whether margins recover from about 28%.
Phosphoric acid and freight cost volatility; geopolitical situation has raised raw material inventory and working capital (214 days). Target is 170-180 days ex-battery.
Greenfield Nandesari plant will carry operating costs at low utilisation, and battery pre-commercial costs will hit P&L before revenue.

Battery business: binding offtakes not yet disclosed; Dahej commissioning scheduled for April 2027; Phase 2 is contingent on binding commitments. Sodium-ion chemistry could be a long-term competitive factor.
key_quotes: Q2 marked our highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA, supported by strong growth in our core business and improvements in both gross margin and EBITDA margin.
Importantly, this expectation is based on customer contracts and new business alone and does not assume a restart of the Fortified Rice program.
I will refrain from giving out too many details today.
So, the goal will be to kind of sustain these margin levels. There would not be any significant change from these margin levels.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the record quarter, with firm guidance on Specialty Ingredients returning to growth in Q3 and Q4 FY27. Cautious and evasive on battery specifics: management declined to give binding offtake volumes, EBITDA margin or capex figures, deferring them to the next call or within two months.

adds.what: 51,000 tpa greenfield Nandesari PFN plant (phosphates, glycinates, gluconates, citrates), US FDA approved
25,000 tpa Dahej battery-grade iron phosphate (Sudeep Advanced Materials) Phase 1

growth.why: Management guides Specialty Ingredients back to positive YoY growth in Q3 and Q4 FY27 on new contracts, and greenfield Nandesari (51,000 tpa, FDA approved) to contribute mainly from Q4 with 10-15% utilisation in FY28; PFN core site at about 80% utilisation, with the Dahej battery plant targeting April 2027, but no quantified offtake yet (binding update expected Q4).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin hit 37.2% vs 34.1% a year ago, but management guides only to sustaining around 37%, with Specialty margin (about 28%) expected to recover toward pre-Q2 levels in Q3-Q4 and greenfield and battery costs starting to hit P&L.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Greenfield Nandesari (51,000 tpa) is already capitalised and FDA approved, with supply flowing from Q4 FY27 (small quantities Q3), and Dahej battery Phase 1 (25,000 tpa) is under construction for April 2027 commercial operations.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: PFN volume grew about 30-35% in Q2 and about 19% in H1, with bisglycinate getting the top capacity allocation, and Specialty returning to positive YoY growth in Q3-Q4 on new contracts; greenfield utilisation only 10-15% in FY28.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Nandesari PFN site is at about 80% utilisation, FY27 capex is about INR77 crore, and Dahej Phase 2 (100,000 tpa, about INR600 crore for the first 100,000 tpa) plus a possible expansion to 200,000 tpa is being discussed, contingent on binding offtakes expected Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides Specialty back to positive YoY growth in Q3-Q4 on new contracts, but it expects margins to be sustained rather than strengthened and the Fortified Rice restart has no visibility, so an upgrade is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fortified Rice restart is uncertain (about 20-25% of Specialty revenue, INR40-50 crore in FY26), and greenfield plus battery pre-commercial costs will hit P&L before revenue, with working capital at 214 days versus a 170-180 day target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Magnesium bisglycinate (about 8-9 US approvals, 2-3x PFN average realisation) is targeted to become a top-3 PFN contributor within 2-3 years with at least INR100 crore potential, and battery-grade iron phosphate commercial supply starts April 2027.

rows.label: Binding battery offtake disclosure
rows.why: Management deferred offtake volumes to the next call or within two months, with binding commitments targeted for Q4 FY27 for Phase 1 of 25,000 tpa.

rows.label: Working capital cycle reduction to 170-180 days
rows.why: Net working capital is at 214 days (30 Sep 2026), similar to March 2026, against a 170-180 day target ex-battery inventory, and battery inventory is being built up ahead of commissioning.

rows.label: NSS recovery to growth and ~30% margin in FY28
rows.why: NSS is flat in FY27 with five customer approvals and about 12 projects in evaluation, targeting growth in line with the core business and EBITDA margin near 30% in FY28.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record quarter, PFN volumes and firm Specialty recovery guidance for Q3-Q4 FY27, but cautious and evasive on battery offtake volumes, battery margins and capex, deferring those to the next call.
